top_story: Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth are signaling a possible sharp escalation against Iran, including threats to destroy power plants unless Tehran reopens the Strait of Hormuz, pushing the confrontation beyond coercive signaling toward openly punitive action. Iranian officials and commanders are framing these threats as an attack on the country’s civilian life and warning that strikes on infrastructure would widen the conflict across the Gulf, where shipping, energy flows, and densely populated urban systems are tightly exposed. In Washington, the focus on electrical grids and other civilian targets is also creating a legal and moral fault line inside the U.S. military, because carrying out such orders could implicate officers in unlawful attacks and war-crimes liability. The deeper risk is that infrastructure warfare would not compel Iranian capitulation so much as harden domestic resistance, deepen civilian suffering, and turn a failed pressure campaign into a broader regional crisis.
